root: ^If you’re so powerful, how come you don’t solve all our crises?

c-0: ^General Alcino: Hah! No shame in asking.
^ Let me fetch a bottle of wine — demons make dreadful company when dry-throated.
c-1: ^General Alcino: Oh, *finally*! A hundred years in this town and someone grows the spine to ask.
^ What, the horns don’t give it away?

c-0: ^General Alcino: Not to you. Not to this town.
^ But make no mistake—I ruled in hell, same as every other lord squabbling over their pit of fire.
^ Torturing thieves, liars, murderers… the usual entertainment.
^General Alcino: And yet… I got tired of it. Imagine finding pity for the most wretched souls humanity ever spat out.
^ That’s when my brothers decided I didn’t belong. “Too soft,” they said. So they exiled me here.
^General Alcino: When I arrived, this was no town — just a lonely tower on a muddy hill.
^ I’ve watched it grow stone by stone, until the screams of the damned feel more dream than memory.

c-2: ^General Alcino: Hah! Took you long enough to ask the obvious.
^General Alcino: My true power has slumbered for millennia—and that’s where I’d prefer it stay.
^ If I so much as use 1% of it, this pleasant little earth under your boots would melt into rivers of lava.
^ Have you ever seen fire fall instead of rain?
^ No? Good. You don’t want to. Believe me.
